1. Kitchen counter (counter_k1) is the primary morning hub for personal items (phones, chargers, water bottles, mugs, notebooks, pens) and shared items (lunchboxes, pans). Why: d00 06:16 and 06:22 observations show high density of these items on counter_k1 while sink_k1 is empty.
2. Residents transition from bedrooms to kitchen/common areas by 06:06. Why: d00 06:06 bedroom_1 empty; d00 06:16 resident_1 in kitchen.
3. Personal items (glasses, books) may remain in bedroom nightstands (nightstand_b1) even when resident is absent. Why: d00 06:06 nightstand_b1 held book_marisol, glasses_marisol while resident_1 was in kitchen.
4. Sink (sink_k1) is not a storage location for personal items during morning routines. Why: d00 06:22 sink_k1 empty despite resident_1 presence and items on adjacent counter.
5. Items can move between counter_k1 and other spots (e.g., mug_talia moved, pan_shared_1 appeared) but counter_k1 remains the anchor. Why: d00 06:16 vs 06:22 counter_k1 contents changed slightly but core items persisted.
6. Early morning (06:00-06:30) is a high-activity period for kitchen use. Why: Multiple observations show resident_1 active in kitchen with many items present.
7. Bedroom desks (desk_b1) are empty in early morning. Why: d00 06:06 desk_b1 empty.
8. Residents are not in bedrooms at 06:06. Why: d00 06:06 bed_b1, desk_b1 empty; resident_1 in kitchen by 06:16.
9. Shared items (lunchboxes, mugs) are prepared in kitchen early morning. Why: d00 06:16 counter_k1 held lunchbox_nico, lunchbox_talia, mug_marisol, mug_talia.
10. Personal electronics (phones, chargers) are kept on kitchen counter during morning. Why: d00 06:16 counter_k1 held phone_nico, phone_talia, charger_marisol, charger_nico.
11. Water bottles are kept on kitchen counter during morning. Why: d00 06:16 counter_k1 held water_bottle_marisol, water_bottle_nico.
12. Notebooks and pens are kept on kitchen counter during morning. Why: d00 06:16 counter_k1 held notebook_marisol, pen_marisol.", "why": "The previous beliefs were too general about 'common areas' and did not explicitly rule out the sink as a storage spot.
